title: Bruce Nickoley vs. Rocky Mountain Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was administratively out of order under SJC Manual 10.1 because the Presbytery action complained of—dissolution of its relationship with Evergreen Church—was also the subject of an appeal already granted and docketed for the January 22–24, 1997, meeting of Presbytery; BCO 43-1 bars a complaint in a judicial case in which an appeal is taken.
first_summary: Bruce Nickoley complained against Rocky Mountain Presbytery over its dissolution of the relationship with Evergreen Church. The SJC determined the complaint out of order: the same matter was already on appeal, and BCO 43-1 forbids a complaint in a judicial case in which an appeal is taken. The appeal was docketed for Presbytery's January 22–24, 1997 meeting. The record gives no merits ruling.
summary: Bruce Nickoley complained against Rocky Mountain Presbytery over its action dissolving the relationship with Evergreen Church. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under SJC Manual 10.1. The same matter was already the subject of an appeal granted to Evergreen Church and docketed for Presbytery's January 22–24, 1997 meeting, and BCO 43-1 provides that no complaint is allowable in a judicial case in which an appeal is taken. No merits ruling was reached.
